answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can work like a lagoon: new identities enter a shallow, low-trust terrace where every attested transaction slowly deepens their water. To reach the mesa — full voting and payout rights — each identity must build a long, unbroken trail of on-chain endorsements from diverse, already-deep peers. Spinning up a thousand fakes is cheap, but farming each one a credible history over months, where every vouch risks slashing if it backs another fake, costs far more than any reward it could drain. History becomes the expensive part; copies become useless.
